runs.tool: nsys profile -t cuda --stats=true (public NVIDIA Nsight Systems), whisper-cli on file 1089-134686-0000 (10.44 s), fp16 models
findings: Kernel-launch overhead is first-order on Orin's CPU: 15-38 us per cudaLaunchKernel, 47,335 launches for one large-v3 file (716 ms API time). GGML_CUDA_GRAPHS is OFF in the default whisper.cpp build (option is marked llama.cpp-only) -> increment 2 = graphs-enabled build.

Format-conversion waste: convert_unary fp16<->fp32 pairs cost ~164 ms/file on turbo (~24% of the encoder pass). Cause located in ggml_cuda_mul_mat_cublas_impl: on SM 8.7 compute_type=F16 with prefer_f32_output=false, so fp32 activations convert to f16 in and the f16 GEMM output converts back to f32 out.
Unfused glue: thousands of 3-12 us elementwise kernels (bin_bcast add/mul, norm, scale, cpy, gelu) per file; each costs more to launch than to run.
Encoder attention: flash_attn_ext_f16<64,64,64> = 4.0 ms x 32 layers on both models; with GEMMs this is the fp16-bound encoder floor (~660-760 ms/file) that dominates e2e after decode shrinks.

runs.note: Owner decision: memory capacity is not the constraint (fp16 peak RSS 4.4 GB of 7 GB), so quantization is recorded as a reference arm and NOT adopted as mainline; mainline is native C/CUDA optimization at fp16 quality.

quality_gate.corpus_wer: no regression in any arm; large-v3 q8/q5 improved 0.00301 -> 0.0015 (fixed one of two baseline errors)
quality_gate.per_file: no file regressed in any arm; large-v3 quant arms fixed 1089-134686-0008; turbo error pattern identical across fp16/q8/q5 (1089-134686-0004, -0016)
quality_gate.resolution_caveat: 665 reference words; one error = 0.15% WER; per-file transcript diffs used below corpus resolution

runs.tool: whisper.cpp rebuilt with -DGGML_CUDA_GRAPHS=ON (build-graphs), A/B vs graphs-off build, adjacent pairs one session
runs.bench_deltas: decode ms/tok flat (55.80 vs 56.04 large, 10.64 vs 10.67 turbo); batchd -6% both (6.53->6.12, 1.12->1.04) within session noise
runs.root_cause: ggml CUDA graphs require a 2-call warmup with unchanged node properties (ggml_backend_cuda_graph_compute); whisper's decode graph changes tensor properties every step (growing KV positions), so warmup never completes and no graph is captured. The option is marked llama.cpp-only upstream for this reason.
runs.lesson: Launch-overhead reduction on whisper must come from reducing kernel count (fusion), not from graph capture.

runs.tool: native CUDA patch (patches/0001-whisper-shape-cuda-fusions.patch) on whisper.cpp 4834a23; A/B = same binary, control GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_FUSION=1 (stock: whisper triggers no other fusion patterns), adjacent runs one session
runs.change: Two whisper-shaped patterns added to ggml-cuda's fusion framework: NORM->MUL->ADD fused into norm_mul_add_f32 (LayerNorm with weight+bias in one kernel, contiguous row-vector gamma/beta), ADD->UNARY(GELU) fused into add_bias_gelu_f32 (row-vector bias). __fmul_rn/__fadd_rn preserve unfused rounding exactly.
runs.gains: large-v3 e2e +3.7%, turbo e2e +6.0%; encoder pass -6.5% / -7.9%; per turbo file norm_mul_add_f32 fires 611x replacing 1,833 kernels, add_bias_gelu_f32 fires 196x, ~1,400 fewer launches of ~7,200
runs.quality_gate: GOLD: all 64 transcripts (32 files x 2 models) byte-identical to stock; corpus WER unchanged 0.00301 both models; RSS unchanged; swap 0
runs.note: single-stream decode bench showed +-8% session noise (ctl 50.6 vs historic 55.8 ms/tok) - e2e on the pinned subset is the decision metric, bench is directional only

runs.tool: native patch in ggml_cuda_mul_mat_cublas_impl: prefer_f32_output forced on (cuBLAS f16xf16->f32, fp32 accumulate, no f16 dst_temp + convert_unary epilogue); A/B same binary via GGML_CUDA_CUBLAS_F32_OUT, adjacent runs one session, on top of increment 3
runs.gains: turbo e2e +4.6%; encoder bench -3.7% (large-v3, 702->676ms) and -5.8% (turbo quick bench 627->590ms); large-v3 e2e neutral (decode-dominated, encoder only ~28% of processing)
runs.quality_gate: GOLD: all 64 transcripts byte-identical to stock despite fp32-accumulate rounding change; WER 0.00301 both models; RSS +18-28 MB (f32 dst buffers) - acceptable at 2.4/4.5 GB of 7 GB
runs.note: session drift visible again: fused-only arm measured 2.925 in the inc3 session and 2.977 as this session's control - only adjacent same-session pairs are compared

runs.tool: native patch: bias pointer threaded through ggml mmf tensor-core kernel writeback (__fadd_rn epilogue) + MUL_MAT->ADD fusion pattern routing to mmf (beam decode) or mmvf fusion args (single column); A/B fused vs GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_FUSION=1, adjacent runs one session, on top of increments 3+4
runs.gains: cumulative fusion pair: large-v3 +7.4% (inc3 pair alone was +3.7%), turbo +5.8% (inc3 alone +6.0%); k_bin_bcast add launches per large-v3 file 17,656 (baseline) -> 4,301; mmf GEMM time unchanged with epilogue folded in (486ms/8,960 calls)
runs.quality_gate: GOLD: all 64 transcripts byte-identical to no-fusion control; WER 0.00301 both models; RSS unchanged
runs.context: decode GEMMs measured at ~85% of the 102 GB/s bandwidth floor (16.6 ms/step vs ~14 ms theoretical for 1.45 GB weights + 0.25 GB cross-KV per step), so decode headroom is glue/launches, not GEMM math

runs.tool: native patch: node->op gates on all fusion pattern checks in ggml_cuda_try_fuse + early-outs in the three MUL_MAT scan loops; A/B = library-isolated snapshot of the increment-5 build (LD_LIBRARY_PATH) vs op-gated build, adjacent runs one session, both arms fully fused
runs.gains: +1.3% large-v3, +1.5% turbo - small but consistent across both models; fusion decisions provably unchanged (gates only skip checks that would fail), transcripts identical by construction and by measurement (0/64 differ)
runs.open_question: whisper-bench single-stream decode is ~8% faster with GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_FUSION=1 (50.6 vs 54.8 ms/tok, reproduced 3 sessions, present in stock whisper.cpp too); op-gating did NOT recover it, so the cost is elsewhere in the fusion machinery (bench-level decode only - e2e beam decode favors fusion). Not yet located.

observations: Encoder cost is nearly identical between the two models (both 32 encoder layers); turbo's advantage is entirely the 4-layer decoder: 10.64 vs 55.85 ms/token single-stream decode.
large-v3 cold model load is 35.8 s for the 3.1 GB fp16 image; any non-resident serving pattern is load-dominated (820 s wall vs 86 s processing across 32 invocations).
Identical corpus WER (0.301%) between models is coincidence: 2 errors each on different files; 11 of 32 raw transcripts differ before normalization.

Battery1: cutting single-stream decode 2.7x (q5) moved turbo e2e only 7.18 -> 7.42 RTFx; the ~660-760 ms per-file encoder pass and per-invocation fixed costs dominate the e2e path once decode shrinks. Native optimization should attack encoder + fixed costs first.
Session drift: fp16 large-v3 measured 2.917 RTFx in the first session and 2.777 in the battery session (~5%); compared arms must run back-to-back in one session.
